res4_variable_analysis.question: What dynamic physiological variable changes venous sinus stent behavior in a way a shunt CANNOT reproduce?

key_architectural_distinction.shunt: Controls CSF FLOW RATE by adjusting valve (CSF→venous drainage). Operates on CSF-venous pressure differential. Does NOT interact with venous outflow capacity.
key_architectural_distinction.static_vss: Controls VENOUS OUTFLOW CAPACITY by maintaining lumen diameter (venous→venous). Fixed diameter → fixed max outflow capacity. Cannot adapt to changing demand.
key_architectural_distinction.adaptive_vss_hypothesis: REGULATES venous outflow capacity by variable diameter/flow element. Can increase or decrease outflow in response to changing physiology.

variables_assessed.name: Trans-stenotic gradient (venous-to-venous)
variables_assessed.ce_013: PARTIALLY independent — venous gradient is different from CSF-venous differential, but both are pressure measurements
variables_assessed.ce_012_risk: Measuring a different gradient is 'more of the same variable'
variables_assessed.verdict: WEAK — risks CE-012 (same variable, different location)

variables_assessed.name: Venous outflow RESERVE (capacity to increase flow when demand increases)
variables_assessed.description: The maximum venous outflow capacity of the stented sinus. A static stent has fixed capacity; if physiological demand exceeds capacity, ICP rises. A shunt CANNOT increase venous outflow — it bypasses the venous system entirely.
variables_assessed.ce_013: PASSES — venous outflow capacity is UPSTREAM of CSF pressure (venous outflow → venous pressure → CSF absorption → CSF pressure). Shunts measure the downstream consequence. VSS would regulate the upstream cause.
variables_assessed.ce_012: PARTIALLY PASSES — 'dynamic venous outflow regulation' is a technical effect that neither shunts (bypass venous system) nor static stents (fixed diameter) can achieve. BUT the mechanism (variable diameter) may face §103 from shape-memory or hydraulic stent art.
variables_assessed.verdict: STRONGEST — genuinely new technical effect (regulatable venous outflow)

variables_assessed.name: Sinus wall-stent interaction (mechanical coupling)
variables_assessed.ce_013: PASSES — this interaction is unique to VSS architecture; shunts do not contact sinus wall
variables_assessed.ce_012: Potentially new, but this is a DEVICE FAILURE mode (restenosis), not a physiological variable to be regulated
variables_assessed.verdict: MODERATE — relevant for monitoring but not for the core technical effect

variables_assessed.name: Pressure-flow hysteresis in venous sinus
variables_assessed.ce_013: UNKNOWN — need to check if downstream of ICP

res4_variable_analysis.strongest_variable: V2 (Venous outflow reserve / regulatable venous outflow capacity)

ce_013_result.question: Is 'venous outflow capacity' causally independent of shunt-measured variables?
ce_013_result.answer: YES — venous outflow capacity is a property of the VENOUS SYSTEM. Shunts measure CSF pressure and CSF-venous differential (downstream consequences). Venous outflow capacity is UPSTREAM of CSF pressure: (venous outflow → venous pressure → CSF absorption → CSF pressure). VSS would regulate the UPSTREAM cause; shunts measure the DOWNSTREAM consequence.
ce_013_result.verdict: PASSES CE-013 — venous outflow capacity is causally independent of (upstream of) shunt-measured variables

ce_012_result.question: Does 'regulatable venous outflow capacity' produce a new technical effect that cannot be achieved by trivial recombination?
ce_012_result.answer: The new technical effect is 'DYNAMIC VENOUS OUTFLOW REGULATION' — the ability to increase or decrease venous outflow capacity in response to changing physiological demand. This is NOT achievable by: (a) shunts (they bypass the venous system — they drain CSF, not regulate venous outflow), (b) static stents (fixed diameter — cannot change capacity post-deployment), (c) Hakim's closed-loop shunt (controls CSF drainage valve, not venous patency). No existing stent can change diameter on demand post-deployment (balloon-expandable = fixed, self-expanding = fixed, bioresorbable = uncontrolled degradation).
ce_012_result.but: The MECHANISM (variable diameter stent) may face §103 from shape-memory alloy, hydraulic, or electromechanical stent art. The technical EFFECT is new, but the mechanism may not be.
ce_012_result.verdict: PARTIALLY PASSES CE-012 — the technical effect is genuinely new (not achievable by existing systems), but the mechanism requires novelty analysis

decision_value_test.question: What can the clinician/device do with adaptive VSS that static VSS or existing shunt CANNOT?
answers: A1: Patient gains weight → venous compression increases → outflow demand increases → static stent insufficient → adaptive stent EXPANDS → prevents ICP rise. (Shunt CANNOT do this — it drains CSF but doesn't address venous outflow capacity.)
A2: Patient loses weight → venous compression decreases → over-drainage risk → adaptive stent CONSTRICTS → prevents low pressure. (Shunt can adjust valve, but stent currently CANNOT adjust.)
A3: Post-VSS monitoring → sensing stent detects restenosis BEFORE symptoms → clinician adjusts stent diameter or plans intervention. (Current practice: wait for symptoms → emergency re-stenting.)
decision_value_test.verdict: MODERATE-HIGH decision value — enables preventive diameter adjustment, bidirectional flow regulation, and restenosis early detection. These are capabilities that NO existing device provides for venous sinus.

what_is_strong: The architectural distinction is REAL: shunts operate on CSF drainage, VSS operates on venous outflow. These are different physical systems.
The technical effect (dynamic venous outflow regulation) is NOT achievable by any existing device.
CE-013 PASSES: venous outflow is upstream of CSF pressure, not a downstream consequence.
Decision value is MODERATE-HIGH: enables preventive adjustment, bidirectional regulation, and early detection.
what_is_uncertain: The MECHANISM (how to make a stent change diameter on demand) is NOT yet defined. Shape-memory, hydraulic, electromechanical are candidates, but each has failure modes (see CE-006 thermal window, CE-011 MRI safety).
§103 risk: combining sensing stent + venous stent + flow regulation + IIH may be argued as obvious by combination.
The prior-art search was keyword-based (12 queries). Full 12-stage destruction (CPC, family, citations) NOT yet performed.
No evidence that changing stent diameter post-deployment is physically feasible in venous sinus (different from arterial — venous wall is thinner, lower pressure, more compliant).
The problem (dynamic physiology) is REAL, but the solution (adaptive VSS) is a HYPOTHESIS, not a demonstrated capability.
honest_assessment.classification: DISCOVERY HYPOTHESIS — NOT promoted. The technical effect is potentially new, but the mechanism, feasibility, and full prior-art analysis are NOT complete.
